lessons: The renewal-deadline off-by-one shipped because both the prose and the calculator restated the fee BAND label (years 7-10) as if it were the DUE DATE (year-7 anniversary). The official Hebrew text says 'lifnei tom hashana hashishit', before the end of the sixth year. Whenever a fee is described by the period it covers, separately record the date it must be paid; the two are not the same field and in Israel they differ by a full year.

The fee table under-quoted because 12 cells said 'see official schedule' rather than a number. A placeholder is indistinguishable from a verified absence. Never ship a placeholder in a fee table; either fetch the number or state that the row does not exist.

The accelerated-examination fee was collapsed from a four-cell matrix into the single applicant-route total (357 + 834 = 1,191). The arithmetic was right and the answer was still incomplete: the third-party route under s.19a(c) costs 17,865 and is a competitive-strategy fact, not merely a fee. When a published fee splits by WHO pays or WHY, enumerate every branch.

The 40% reduction had three independent errors in one paragraph, all of which came from paraphrasing a practitioner summary instead of the statutory row. The official text carries eligibility, the first-application condition, and the scope of application in a single sentence. Read the fee notice row itself, not a law-firm restatement of it.

gov.il HTML pages return HTTP 403 to WebFetch, which reads as a dead link and invites a guess. The underlying BlobFolder PDF downloads cleanly with curl and has a text layer extractable with 'pdftotext -layout'. Try the PDF before concluding a gov.il source is unreachable, and never mark a 403 as broken.

Scope was drawn around the content rather than around the user's question. The skill excluded designs and trademarks while already parsing the very fee notice that contains both, and while the founder persona it targets routinely needs them. An exclusion is only honest if it survives being re-read next to the user's actual question.
